gaps.sentence: He completed the marathon despite being ___ breath.
gaps.explanation: 'out of breath' = breathing fast from effort.

gaps.sentence: The museum is open to the public ___ appointment only.
The proposal is still ___ the table — nothing has been decided.
gaps.explanation: 'On the table' = offered and still being considered.

gaps.sentence: The matter went completely ___ my head — I cannot recall a thing.
gaps.explanation: 'Over one's head' = too complicated to understand.

gaps.sentence: Everything was left ___ the care of the next-door neighbours.
gaps.explanation: 'In the care of' = looked after by.'

gaps.sentence: I did it ___ my own initiative — nobody asked me.
gaps.explanation: 'of one's own initiative' = without being asked.

gaps.sentence: She succeeded in ___ of repeated setbacks.
The proposal was rejected ___ a single vote.
gaps.explanation: 'by a single vote / by two goals' — the margin takes 'by'.
